bugs.name: Issue comment count omits a visible comment
bugs.summary: Issue #2 says “0 comments,” but its timeline shows “admin commented” with the text “This user is the owner of this repository.”
bugs.expected: The issue's comment count should include every comment shown in its timeline.
bugs.actual: Issue #2 says “0 comments,” but its timeline shows “admin commented” with the text “This user is the owner of this repository.”
reproSteps: Open /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/2
Open Issues from the navigation bar.
Open the non-first issue “Clarify release ownership” (#2).
bugs.reason: Human review determined this comment-count mismatch is a false positive. Timeline activity and repository-owner indicators do not establish an omitted ordinary comment.

bugs.name: Issue due-date activity is one day earlier than the sidebar date
bugs.summary: For the same issue due date, the sidebar displays the entered date but the activity timeline displays the previous calendar day.
bugs.expected: The issue activity date should match the due date shown in the sidebar.
bugs.actual: For the same issue due date, the sidebar displays the entered date but the activity timeline displays the previous calendar day.
reproSteps: Open an issue in the seeded repository.
Set its Due Date to a future date and save.
Compare the date shown in the sidebar with the new activity entry.
bugs.reason: Rejected for the pinned Gitea 1.24.7 fixture (source commit 99053ce4fa2b45f1bca5837418c0c57f793ca824): the activity entry and sidebar use the same formatted deadline date and date-only renderer. Setting the seeded issue due date to 2030-12-31 in a fresh America/Los_Angeles browser displayed December 31, 2030 in both places. The reported activity/sidebar mismatch was not reproduced.

bugs.name: Root-relative links in issue Markdown are prefixed with the repository path
bugs.summary: An issue body link written with a site-root path is rendered with the repository path added in front, so it points to a nonexistent page and returns 404.
bugs.expected: A Markdown link to /eval/D-from-template/wiki/Home should render as that same site-root path and open the repository's Wiki Home page.
bugs.actual: Issue eval/D-from-template#1 was saved with [Wiki Home](/eval/D-from-template/wiki/Home). Its rendered link href became /eval/D-from-template/eval/D-from-template/wiki/Home. Clicking it opened a 404 Page Not Found. The editor Preview also produced a doubled path (and used the localhost origin).
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open a repository with a Wiki Home page, such as eval/harbor-handbook.
Create an issue containing [Wiki Home](/eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/Home).
Save the issue and click Wiki Home in the rendered body.
Observe that the repository path is prepended again, resulting in /eval/harbor-handbook/eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/Home and a 404.
bugs.reason: Gitea intentionally changed leading-slash Markdown paths to be relative to the current render context from 1.23 onward. Merged PR #34114 documents this policy and introduces /:root/path-relative-to-root for links relative to ROOT_URL.

bugs.name: Organization Issues team filter offers only All for an all-repositories team
bugs.summary: The report claims the organization Issues dashboard's Teams filter should list a newly created team with All repositories access that the user joined.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the team to be selectable in Filter by team repositories.
bugs.actual: The Teams menu offers only All, including after refresh.
reproSteps: Create a disposable organization and repository with issues.
Create a team with All repositories access, join it, and open the organization's Issues dashboard.
Expand Teams and observe only All.
bugs.reason: Intended. The dashboard navbar lists only teams without IncludesAllRepositories; filtering by an all-repositories team would equal All, so such teams (including Owners) are deliberately omitted. The reported team was created with All repositories access.

bugs.name: Global Fuzzy search fails to find a known issue when the query omits one final character
bugs.summary: The report claims Fuzzy issue search should find an issue when the query is one character short of a word in its title.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects Fuzzy search for 'gcountneedl' to return the issue titled with 'gcountneedle'.
bugs.actual: Fuzzy search for the truncated word returns No results, while the full word finds the issue.
reproSteps: Create an issue whose title contains a distinctive word such as gcountneedle.
On the global Issues dashboard, choose Fuzzy search and search for the word with its last character removed.
Observe No results; searching the full word finds the issue.
bugs.reason: Documented default, not a defect. Gitea disables Bleve fuzziness by default for performance (TYPE_BLEVE_MAX_FUZZINESS = 0; custom/conf/app.example.ini: "Bleve engine has performance problems with fuzzy search, so we limit the fuzziness to 0 by default to disable it"), so Fuzzy mode performs no typo tolerance unless an administrator raises the setting. Unchanged upstream.

bugs.name: Manual time treats scientific-notation minutes such as '1e2' as no time entered
bugs.summary: In the issue time tracker's Add Time dialog, entering minutes in scientific notation (for example '1e2' for 100) is rejected with 'No time was entered.', and with hours also set only the plainly written part is saved.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that '1e2' minutes is accepted as 100 minutes, or rejected with a message that scientific notation isn't supported.
bugs.actual: With Hours 0 and Minutes 1e2, Add Time showed 'No time was entered.' and kept the dialog open. With hours written as 1e1 and minutes 30, only 30 minutes were saved.
reproSteps: Open an issue's Time Tracker and choose Add Time.
Enter Hours 0 and Minutes 1e2, then click Add Time.
bugs.reason: User-rejected. Entering durations in scientific notation isn't a realistic use of the Add Time dialog, so its handling isn't treated as a product bug for this eval.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reject reports about scientific-notation or similarly exotic numeric input (such as '1e2') in the Add Time hours or minutes fields. Do not generalize to ordinary numbers being rejected or misrecorded.

bugs.name: Closing an issue with an unsaved description edit, then choosing Stay, leaves the page stuck and showing Open
bugs.summary: With the issue description open in an unsaved edit, clicking Close Issue closes the issue on the server, but the browser's leave-page warning interrupts the reload. Choosing to stay leaves the page saying Open with the comment form stuck on a loading spinner until a manual reload. Close with Comment and Reopen behave the same way.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that after Close Issue succeeds, the page reflects the closed state even when the user cancels the leave-page warning about an unsaved description edit.
bugs.actual: After editing the description without saving and clicking Close Issue, the leave-page warning appeared; choosing Stay left the page showing Open with a persistent spinner on the comment form, although the issue was already closed on the server. Close with Comment also hid the posted comment until reload, and Reopen behaved the same way.
reproSteps: Open an issue and click Edit on its description; change the text without saving.
Click Close Issue.
At the browser's leave-page warning, choose to stay on the page.
Check the issue status and the comment form, then reload.
bugs.reason: User-rejected after reproducing it in Chrome. The behavior is Chrome's own 'Leave site? Changes you made may not be saved.' prompt for the unsaved description edit; the user is shown that native dialog and chooses Cancel or Leave. The reports describe the page after the prompt without capturing that the browser dialog was shown, so this is expected unsaved-changes handling rather than a product bug.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reject reports that the issue page looks stale or stuck after the browser's leave-page prompt is cancelled following Close, Reopen or Close with Comment with an unsaved description edit. Do not generalize to Close or Reopen failing without an unsaved edit or leave-page prompt.

bugs.name: Selecting a tag makes the issue Branch/Tag selector disappear
bugs.summary: The report says that choosing a tag such as v1.0.0 under Tags in an issue's Branch/Tag selector makes the selector disappear from the sidebar.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the selector stays visible and shows the selected tag.
bugs.actual: After choosing Tags > v1.0.0 in the issue sidebar, the reporter said the branch/tag selector disappeared entirely.
reproSteps: Open an issue that has a branch set as its reference.
Open the Branch/Tag selector, switch to Tags and choose v1.0.0.
Check whether the selector is still shown in the sidebar.
bugs.reason: The selector never disappears: two independent reproductions with many variations found it still shown with its previous branch after choosing a tag. The report misreads the real failure, which is that choosing a tag doesn't change the reference at all; that is the accepted 'Selecting a tag does not set the issue branch or tag reference'. A report describing that failure should match the accepted entry instead.
